stem:
Charu stands at the same small distance in front of three mirrors at home.
Mirror P shows her face erect and the same size as her face.
Mirror Q shows her face erect and larger than her face.
Mirror R shows her face erect and smaller than her face.

options.text: P is plane, Q is concave (object close), R is convex.
P is convex, Q is plane, R is concave.
P is plane, Q is convex, R is concave.
P, Q, and R are all plane mirrors because each image is erect.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A plane mirror keeps size; a close object at a concave mirror can look erect and enlarged; a convex mirror gives an erect smaller image.

teacher.key_rationale: Same-size erect image marks a plane mirror. Close-object erect enlarged image marks concave. Erect diminished image marks convex. Erect alone does not make every mirror plane.
